author: Linnaeus, 1766
status: 나그네새 수천 마리 · 여름철새 수백 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록
habitat: 서남 해안 갯벌, 강 하구, 물 고인 농경지, 습초지
summary: 봄과 가을에 비교적 흔히 지나가는 나그네새이지만, 세계적으로는 매우 드문 새이다. 서남해안 갯벌과 강 하구, 물 고인 농경지와 습한 풀밭에 내려앉아 주로 게를 잡고 다른 갑각류와 갯지렁이도 즐겨 먹는다. 세계자연보전연맹 적색목록에 취약(VU)으로 올라 있고 전 세계 개체수는 32,000마리쯤으로 추정되는데, 서식지 파괴와 오염으로 크게 줄고 있으며 국내 갯벌 매립으로 중간 기착지가 줄어든 것도 위협이 된다. 시베리아 동북부와 중국 동북부에서 번식하고 필리핀, 뉴기니, 호주에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Far Eastern Curlew (Numenius madagascariensis), adult, as seen on Korean south-west coast mudflats in April–May and August–September: whole bird warm buff-brown; head plain and finely streaked, without crown stripes; neck, breast and flanks buff, densely streaked dark brown, the streaking continuing onto a buff (not white) belly. Upperparts brown, feathers dark-centred with rufous-buff edges and notches. Back and rump brown like the mantle; tail brown with dark bars. Underwing coverts and axillaries densely barred dark brown. Bill extremely long, blackish with a pinkish base to the lower mandible. Eye dark. Legs bluish-grey.
art.pose: walking on a tidal mudflat with a crab in its bill
art.scene: Korean south-west coast tidal mudflat at a river mouth during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view walking on mud: extremely long, evenly decurved bill, plain streaked buff-brown head, warm buff-brown body streaked dark brown down to the belly, long bluish-grey legs
adult, in flight seen from above: uniform brown upperparts, brown back and rump with no white wedge, barred brown tail
adult, in flight seen from below: underwing coverts and axillaries densely barred dark brown, buff-brown streaked body
adult female and male, head detail side by side in side view: the female's bill clearly longer than the male's, both evenly decurved, blackish with a pinkish base below
art.build: Very large shorebird, 58.5–61.5cm, the largest curlew, a little bigger and longer-billed than Eurasian Curlew. Small head, long neck, long legs. Bill extremely long, about three times the head length, decurved smoothly along its whole length; the female's bill is clearly longer than the male's. Legs long, bluish-grey. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight uniformly brown above with no white on the back or rump, and with densely brown-barred underwings that look dark below.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump or a white wedge up the back — that is Eurasian Curlew.
Do not paint white, unmarked underwing coverts or a white belly (Eurasian Curlew).
Do not paint crown stripes (Whimbrel) or a bill kinked only near the tip.
Do not paint cold grey tones; this species is warm buff-brown.
